thread:
neha: heads up — after the provider bump in main (cloud-provider v3.2 -> v3.4) gitops applied and we ended up recreating the eu-west-1 gpu nodepool. pods evicted, short capacity hole.

infra-bot: PR <https://git.redwood.dev/p/infra/merge/4321|infra/merge/4321> created by @neha: 'pin cloud-provider and add compat shim' :github:

sam: wait — which envs saw the recreation? prod only? staging?

neha: prod eu-west-1 and staging eu-west-1. ap-southeast-1 untouched so far. The provider change altered default naming of "node_pool_name" in our module, gitops auto-prune removed the old resource and created new one. We lost ~6 GPU nodes for ~12m.

jess: did KMS/secrets rotate at the same time? wondering if helm diffs triggered too.

neha: KMS rotation was yesterday but unrelated; helm releases were fine. The issue is the tf module schema change — name attr default changed. Diff looked like:```
- name = "redwood-gpu-pool-eu"
+ name = "redwood-gpu-pool-eu-v2"
```

liam: ok — quick mitigation plan: 1) pin provider in root module 2) terraform state mv old -> new OR revert provider bump in gitops 3) do a graceful cordon/drain then scale back up. Example commands:```
# pin provider
provider "cloud" {
  version = ">= 3.1, < 3.3"
}
# move state if already created
terraform state mv module.old_gpu_pool.module.gpu_resource module.gpu_pool.gpu_resource
# cordon & drain
kubectl -n gpu-system cordon <node-name>
kubectl -n gpu-system drain <node-name> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```

sam: can we do a targeted apply against the gpu module only to avoid touching other resources?

neha: yes — `terraform apply -target=module.gpu_pool` after pinning. I'm preparing a PR to pin provider and add an integration test to assert node_pool_name is stable.

oncall-nyc: FYI I did the node cordon/drain for two nodes and forced a restore of pods to taint-free nodes. Pod eviction logs: ```Evicted: Pod gpu-trainer-7 - Node: ip-10-0-2-45 - Reason: NodeReplaced```

jess: cost question — how bad was the spike?

neha: rough billing alert estimate: ~2k USD over 12m due to on-demand fallbacks + cluster autoscaler thrash. billing-bot nailed us: "High GPU spend — eu-west-1" alert at 12:04 UTC.

liam: longer-term: module should include explicit name arg (no implicit defaults), and CI should run a plan check that validates stable resource names. Also add a canary rollout for provider bumps: upgrade in ap-southeast-1 first.

neha: agreed. PR description includes: pin provider, add terraform plan check in CI, add canary script to rollout in ap-southeast-1 prior to global bump.

infra-bot: PR <https://git.redwood.dev/p/infra/merge/4321|infra/merge/4321> merged to main by @sam. Canary scheduled: ap-southeast-1 on 2026-05-02T03:00Z. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks everyone — follow-up action items: neha to add plan-check CI, liam to write canary playbook, oncall-nyc to add a short runbook for nodepool drift. I'll open a short postmortem doc after the dust settles. :memo:
